report_md:
# Breadth — development report

**Verdict: fail.** The RSP/SPY breadth state earns **35.62% CAGR / 64.66% max
DD / 1.00 Sharpe** at 1 bp over 2016-2023. It misses the published TQQQ CAGR
bar (36.72%) by 1.10 pp, falls to 32.01% at 5 bp and 27.63% at 10 bp, and has a
negative 2022-2023 subperiod (-12.61%). The signal is distinguishable from the
existing winners and from a QQQ trend proxy, and the placebo is positive, but
the family is not an above-TQQQ winner. 2024-2026 is untouched.

## Development metrics

| Cost | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | Vol | Exposure | Fills | Turnover |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 bp | 35.62% | 64.66% | 1.00 | 1.46 | 37.5% | 100.0% | 539 | 2,877x |
| 5 bp | 32.01% | 66.20% | 0.93 | 1.36 | 37.5% | 100.0% | 539 | 2,487x |
| 10 bp | 27.63% | 68.11% | 0.84 | 1.22 | 37.5% | 100.0% | 539 | 2,080x |

There are **539 fills across 270 independent fill days** (about 68 fills and
34 events per year), well above the activity floor. Average weights are
**42.3% QQQ, 24.1% TQQQ, 33.6% BIL**.

The cost drag is 8.0 pp from 1 bp to 10 bp, the largest of the three families.
The RSP/SPY 20-day leg crosses its threshold frequently, and the full-book
state changes are expensive.

## Subperiods and years

| Window | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 40.95% | 22.50% | 1.44 |
| 2020-2021 | 92.19% | 28.90% | 1.78 |
| 2022-2023 | -12.61% | 63.62% | 0.03 |

| Year | Return |
|---|---:|
| 2016 | +13.4% |
| 2017 | +18.8% |
| 2018 | +71.4% |
| 2019 | +66.6% |
| 2020 | +233.0% |
| 2021 | +15.4% |
| 2022 | -57.2% |
| 2023 | +82.5% |

The family worked well in 2016-2021, then broke in 2022. The breadth signal
turned defensive too late and then whipsawed; 2022 is -57.2% and the 2022-2023
subperiod is negative. 2023 recovers +82.5%, but not enough to repair the
subperiod. Excluding 2023, the CAGR is **30.37%** with a 0.86 Sharpe.

This is the clearest failure mode of the three: the economic object is real,
but the regime timing failed in the one period where a defensive signal should
have paid.

## Plateau (8 pre-registered cells)

| Windows | TQQQ z | BIL z | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills | Turnover |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **20/60** | **+0.50** | **-0.50** | **35.62%** | **64.7%** | **1.00** | **539** | **2,877x** |
| 20/60 | +0.50 | -0.75 | 30.55% | 69.9% | 0.89 | 499 | 2,305x |
| 20/60 | +0.75 | -0.50 | 38.89% | 51.1% | 1.13 | 519 | 2,674x |
| 20/60 | +0.75 | -0.75 | 33.70% | 54.2% | 1.01 | 479 | 2,047x |
| 20 only | +0.50 | -0.50 | 37.23% | 68.6% | 1.04 | 683 | 3,400x |
| 20 only | +0.75 | -0.75 | 31.43% | 67.8% | 0.97 | 623 | 2,635x |
| 60 only | +0.50 | -0.50 | 29.90% | 69.1% | 0.86 | 433 | 2,212x |
| 60 only | +0.75 | -0.75 | 39.78% | 44.6% | 1.10 | 467 | 2,979x |

Three cells clear the 1 bp CAGR bar: the 20/60 blend at `+0.75/-0.50` (38.89%),
the 20-only at `+0.50/-0.50` (37.23%), and the 60-only at `+0.75/-0.75`
(39.78%). The primary is just below the bar. But every passing cell is a
different corner of the grid, the range is wide (29.90% to 39.78%), and none
of the passing cells is the pre-registered centre. This is parameter-sensitive,
not a plateau.

The 60-only `+0.75/-0.75` cell is the best (39.78% / 44.6% / 1.10), but it is a
slower, stricter corner; it still fails at 10 bp (32.61% in the development
screen). It is reported as a sensitivity, not promoted to the headline after
the fact.

## Placebo and static attribution

* **Circular-shift placebo (100 shifts):** median CAGR 16.4%, 95th percentile
  34.8%; the real 35.62% is at the 96th percentile. Median placebo Sharpe 0.60
  vs the real 1.00 (90th percentile). Median placebo max DD 58.3% vs the real
  64.7%.
* **Static book at the average weights (42.3/24.1/33.6):** 20.04% CAGR / 42.3%
  DD / 0.86 Sharpe. The timing adds **15.58 pp** of CAGR and 0.15 Sharpe.

The placebo says the dates carry information, but the static comparison also
shows the timing is not a free lunch: the dynamic strategy takes more
drawdown than the static mix in this sample.

## Correlation to the nine current winners

| Winner | Correlation |
|---|---:|
| ratio-froth | 0.376 |
| vol-scaled-crash-stop | 0.560 |
| relative-value-tqqq | 0.595 |
| fomc-opex-window | 0.506 |
| family-session-timing | 0.531 |
| family-short-reversal | 0.629 |
| family-rebalance-flow | 0.624 |
| family-intraday-microstructure-day | 0.483 |
| family-ml-microstructure | 0.579 |

Range **0.38 to 0.63**. The highest are `family-short-reversal` (0.629) and
`family-rebalance-flow` (0.624); the lowest is `ratio-froth` (0.376). No
correlation approaches 0.95. Daily-return correlation with the other two new
families is 0.37 (sector) and 0.51 (crypto).

A same-map **QQQ 20/60 momentum** control (`+/-0.50`, TQQQ/BIL/QQQ) earns
18.55% CAGR / 63.7% DD / 0.72 Sharpe and correlates only **0.376** with this
strategy. Breadth is the most orthogonal of the three families to a QQQ trend
proxy.

## Kill criteria

| Criterion | Result | Pass? |
|---|---|---:|
| 1 bp CAGR > 36.72% | 35.62% | **no** |
| 1 bp max DD < 82.29% | 64.66% | yes |
| 10 bp CAGR > 36.72% | 27.63% | **no** |
| Placebo percentile >= 90% | 96% | yes |
| Max winner correlation <= 0.95 | 0.629 | yes |
| >= 100 fills / >= 30 events | 539 / 270 | yes |
| No negative subperiod | 2022-2023 -12.61% | **no** |
| Static blend not within 1 pp | 20.04% vs 35.62% | yes |
| Causality audit | 25/25 perturb, 25/25 mapping | yes |

Three kills fire: the 1 bp CAGR bar, the 10 bp cost bar, and the negative
2022-2023 subperiod. The verdict is **fail**.

## Caveats

* **The primary fails by 1.1 pp at 1 bp.** This is not a rounding issue; the
  5 bp and 10 bp results are materially worse.
* **2022 is the failure.** The signal did not turn defensive early enough and
  then whipsawed; -57.2% is worse than the strategy's own static mix.
* **The plateau is parameter-sensitive.** The passing cells are scattered
  corners, and the best cell is a slower 60-day variant that also fails at
  10 bp.
* **Breadth can stay narrow for a long time.** The 2023 mega-cap rally is the
  obvious counterexample; the strategy recovered, but the 2022-2023 subperiod
  is still negative.
* **2016 is partly a warm-up year.** The 60-day z-score needs 120 observations,
  so early 2016 is QQQ; +13.4% is not a full TQQQ year.
* **Same-session ETF close.** RSP/SPY close at 16:00 ET, the same close used
  for the decision; the fill is the next session's open.
* **Development only.** No 2024-2026 data was read.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd research/new/family-breadth
python strategy.py        # rewrites result.json
```

`build_weights(ts, opens, closes)` returns `(n, 3)` minute weights and accepts
either the shared minute panel or a daily panel. The development guard rejects
panels extending past 2023-12-29 unless the caller supplies `end`.
hypothesis_md:
# family-breadth — hypothesis and pre-registration

**Slug:** `family-breadth`
**Family:** breadth (equal-weight vs cap-weight)
**Development window:** 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29 only. 2024-2026 is not
loaded or inspected by the development run.
**Benchmark bar:** TQQQ 36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD / 0.82 Sharpe (published
1-minute-mark bar). TQQQ on this panel is 36.15% / 82.29% / 0.80.

## 1. Mechanism

An index can rise while most of its constituents do not. The RSP/SPY ratio
measures that distinction directly: RSP is the equal-weight S&P 500, SPY is
the cap-weight S&P 500. When RSP keeps up with or beats SPY, the rally is
broad and the marginal stock is participating. When SPY pulls away from RSP,
the index is being carried by a small number of mega-caps and breadth is
narrowing.

Broad breadth is a risk-appetite state: more stocks are trending, drawdowns
are absorbed by rotation rather than by index-level de-risking, and a 3x
Nasdaq wrapper is better compensated. Narrow breadth is a fragile state: the
index can look strong while the median stock is weak, and the eventual
unwind is often index-level. The strategy therefore holds TQQQ when breadth is
broad, QQQ in the neutral band, and BIL when narrowing is severe.

The primary object is the **RSP/SPY relative return**, not the QQQ price trend
and not the QQQ/SPY relative-strength ratio used by the existing
`qqq-spy-relative` family. The 20-day leg captures a fresh rotation; the
60-day leg confirms a breadth regime. Both are z-scored against their own
trailing 252-session distributions.

## 2. Exact rules

All inputs use daily closes through session `t`. The target is set at the close
of `t` and executed at the first bar open of `t+1`. The shared 2% band applies.

Let `R_t = log(RSP_t) - log(SPY_t)`.

1. `m20_t = R_t - R_{t-20}` and `m60_t = R_t - R_{t-60}`.
2. `z20_t` is the z-score of `m20_t` against its trailing 252 observations
   (minimum 120); `z60_t` is the same for `m60_t`.
3. `score_t = (z20_t + z60_t) / 2`.
4. State:
   * **TQQQ** if `score_t >= +0.50`;
   * **BIL** if `score_t <= -0.50`;
   * **QQQ** otherwise.
5. During the z-score warm-up (score not finite), hold **QQQ**, never TQQQ.
6. Weights are long-only fractions of equity and sum to 1.

## 3. Data, decision clock, and causality

| Item | Choice |
|---|---|
| Signal | RSP and SPY adjusted daily closes from `data/external/` |
| Execution | local 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ/BIL panel via `research/bt.py` |
| Session calendar | QQQ regular sessions; external series reindexed/ffilled |
| Decision | close of session `t` (RSP/SPY close 16:00 ET, same session close) |
| Fill | first bar open of `t+1` |
| Costs | 1 bp headline, 5 bp and 10 bp reported |
| Band | 2% notional |
| Lag | none for RSP/SPY: their official close is stamped at the same 16:00 ET close used for the decision, and the fill is the next open |

The development run uses a panel that ends 2023-12-29. The external loader
reindexes to that panel's sessions, so no 2024-2026 price enters the signal or
the performance. A future-value perturbation audit replaces every RSP/SPY
value after the decision date with garbage and confirms that the target at
that date does not change.

## 4. Why this is not an existing family

* Not `qqq-spy-relative`: that family uses QQQ vs SPY, a Nasdaq-vs-broad
  relative-strength ratio. Here the pair is RSP vs SPY, equal-weight vs
  cap-weight, which measures **breadth**, not Nasdaq leadership.
* Not `ratio-froth` or `relative-value-tqqq`: there is no TQQQ/QQQ ratio, no
  ratio momentum, and no QQQ moving-average gate.
* Not `family-sector-rotation`: that family uses XLK/XLU (growth vs
  defensive); this one uses RSP/SPY (equal-weight vs cap-weight).
* Not `family-beta-rotation`: no covariance or beta is estimated.
* Not a volatility target, drawdown event, calendar clock, opening-range
  signal, or ML model. The RSP/SPY ratio is the primary object, not a filter
  layered on a QQQ price trend.
* The 252-session window is only a standardization lookback for the 20/60-day
  relative return; it is not a 100-250 day price-trend gate.
* The ratio is an external cross-sectional series; QQQ is only the traded
  asset and the neutral state.

## 5. Pre-registered 8-cell sensitivity grid

The grid includes the primary, three threshold neighbours at the 20/60 blend,
and the two single-horizon alternatives at two settings.

| Cell | Windows | TQQQ z | BIL z |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| **1 (primary)** | **20/60 blend** | **+0.50** | **-0.50** |
| 2 | 20/60 blend | +0.50 | -0.75 |
| 3 | 20/60 blend | +0.75 | -0.50 |
| 4 | 20/60 blend | +0.75 | -0.75 |
| 5 | 20 only | +0.50 | -0.50 |
| 6 | 20 only | +0.75 | -0.75 |
| 7 | 60 only | +0.50 | -0.50 |
| 8 | 60 only | +0.75 | -0.75 |

Fixed: 252-session z-window, 120 minimum observations, QQQ as the neutral
state, BIL as the defensive state. The primary is the centre of the mechanism,
not the best cell in the grid.

## 6. Falsifiers (pre-registered)

The family is killed if any of the following holds on the development window:

1. 1 bp CAGR <= 36.72% or 1 bp max DD >= 82.29% (the published TQQQ bar).
2. 10 bp CAGR <= 36.72% (the edge is a cost artefact).
3. The circular-shift placebo CAGR percentile is below 90%.
4. Daily-return correlation with any current family winner is above 0.95.
5. Fewer than 100 fills or fewer than 30 independent fill events.
6. Any of the three subperiods (2016-2019, 2020-2021, 2022-2023) has a
   negative CAGR.
7. A static book at the strategy's average weights matches the 1 bp CAGR
   within 1 percentage point (the timing adds nothing).
8. The future-value perturbation audit fails on any sampled date, or the
   close-to-next-open mapping audit fails (a causality bug).

The verdict is `dev_pass` only if all eight checks pass. A marginal 1 bp pass
with a 10 bp fail is still a fail: the family is not an above-TQQQ winner.

## 7. Expected effect

| metric | expectation |
|---|---|
| CAGR (1 bp) | 30-40% |
| max DD | 50-70% |
| Sharpe | 0.9-1.1 |
| average TQQQ weight | 0.20-0.30 |
| average QQQ weight | 0.35-0.50 |
| correlation to winners | 0.40-0.65 |

If the result is in these ranges with a positive placebo and a materially
worse static blend, the RSP/SPY object carries information. The main risk is
regime asymmetry: narrow breadth can persist for a long time in a mega-cap
rally (notably 2023), so the defensive state can be early and expensive. The
report states whether that risk materialised.

code:
"""family-breadth -- equal-weight vs cap-weight breadth times TQQQ.

Primary object: the RSP/SPY relative return.  When equal-weight RSP keeps up
with or beats cap-weight SPY, the rally is broad and the strategy holds TQQQ.
When SPY pulls away from RSP, breadth is narrowing and the strategy holds QQQ
in the neutral band and BIL when narrowing is severe.

The signal is the average of the 20-day and 60-day relative-return z-scores,
each z-scored against its own trailing 252-session distribution.

Decision clock: RSP/SPY closes are 16:00 ET, the same session close used for
the decision; the target is filled at the next session's first bar open.
Long only, weights sum to 1, 2% band.

Run ``python strategy.py`` from this directory to regenerate ``result.json``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
import ext_harness as H

SLUG = "family-breadth"
FAMILY = "breadth"
PRIMARY = "RSP/SPY 20/60-day relative-return z-score"

END = H.END

PARAMS = {
    "windows": (20, 60),
    "z_window": 252,
    "min_periods": 120,
    "tqqq_z": 0.50,
    "bil_z": -0.50,
}

# 8-cell sensitivity grid: the primary, three threshold neighbours at the
# 20/60 blend, and the 20-only / 60-only alternatives at two settings.
PLATEAU = [
    {"windows": (20, 60), "tqqq_z": 0.50, "bil_z": -0.50},
    {"windows": (20, 60), "tqqq_z": 0.50, "bil_z": -0.75},
    {"windows": (20, 60), "tqqq_z": 0.75, "bil_z": -0.50},
    {"windows": (20, 60), "tqqq_z": 0.75, "bil_z": -0.75},
    {"windows": (20,), "tqqq_z": 0.50, "bil_z": -0.50},
    {"windows": (20,), "tqqq_z": 0.75, "bil_z": -0.75},
    {"windows": (60,), "tqqq_z": 0.50, "bil_z": -0.50},
    {"windows": (60,), "tqqq_z": 0.75, "bil_z": -0.75},
]


def _score(ext: pd.DataFrame, windows) -> pd.Series:
    rel = np.log(ext["RSP"]) - np.log(ext["SPY"])
    parts = [H.rolling_z(rel.diff(int(w)), PARAMS["z_window"],
                         PARAMS["min_periods"])
             for w in windows]
    return sum(parts) / len(parts)


def make_targets(ext: pd.DataFrame, params: dict | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    s = _score(ext, p["windows"])
    return H.state_weights(s, float(p["tqqq_z"]), float(p["bil_z"]))


def _limit(end):
    return pd.Timestamp(end) if end is not None else pd.Timestamp(END)


def _check_window(ts, limit) -> None:
    last = pd.Timestamp(ts[-1])
    if last.tzinfo is not None:
        last = last.tz_localize(None)
    if last.normalize() > limit:
        raise ValueError(
            "panel extends past the development window "
            f"{limit.date()}; 2024-2026 is not loaded")


def build_weights(ts, opens, closes, params: dict | None = None,
                  end=None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Minute weights; targets at session close t fill at t+1's open."""
    limit = _limit(end)
    _check_window(ts, limit)
    ext = H.aligned(ts, ["RSP", "SPY"], end=limit)
    return H.to_minutes(ts, make_targets(ext, params))


def main() -> None:
    ts, o, c = H.load_panel()
    ext = H.aligned(ts, ["RSP", "SPY"])
    targets = make_targets(ext)
    ev = H.evaluate(ts, o, c, targets, n_placebo=100)
    st = ev["stats"]["1bp"]
    kills = H.kill_checks(ev)
    plateau = H.plateau(ts, o, c,
                        lambda p: make_targets(ext, p), PLATEAU)
    causality = {
        "future_value_perturbation": H.perturb_audit(
            ext, make_targets, cutoff_offset=0),
        "close_to_next_open_mapping": H.mapping_audit(ts, targets),
    }
    ctrl_st, ctrl_ret = H.trend_control(ts, o, c, 0.50, -0.50)
    trend_control = {
        "name": "QQQ 20/60 momentum, same three-state map",
        "cagr": ctrl_st["cagr"],
        "max_drawdown": ctrl_st["max_drawdown"],
        "sharpe": ctrl_st["sharpe"],
        "corr_to_strategy": float(ev["_daily_ret"].corr(ctrl_ret)),
    }
    i = H.bt.start_index(ts, H.START)
    bench = H.bt.benchmark(c[i:, 1], ts[i:], H.BARS_PER_YEAR)
    payload = {
        "slug": SLUG,
        "family": FAMILY,
        "primary_object": PRIMARY,
        "dev": st,
        "windows": {"dev": {"1bp": ev["stats"]["1bp"],
                            "5bp": ev["stats"]["5bp"],
                            "10bp": ev["stats"]["10bp"]}},
        "window": {"dev": [H.START, H.END], "holdout": "not loaded"},
        "benchmark": {
            "tqqq_panel": bench,
            "tqqq_published_bar": H.TQQQ_BAR,
        },
        "params": {k: (list(v) if isinstance(v, tuple) else v)
                   for k, v in PARAMS.items()},
        "stats": ev["stats"],
        "events": ev["events"],
        "activity": {"fills": st["fills"], "events": ev["events"],
                     "fills_per_year": st["fills"] / st["years"],
                     "events_per_year": ev["events"] / st["years"]},
        "yearly": ev["yearly"],
        "subperiods": ev["subperiods"],
        "corr_winners": ev["corr_winners"],
        "corr_range": [min(ev["corr_winners"].values()),
                       max(ev["corr_winners"].values())],
        "avg_weights": ev["avg_weights"],
        "static_avg_weights": ev["static_avg_weights"],
        "plateau": plateau,
        "placebo": ev["placebo"],
        "causality_audit": causality,
        "trend_control": trend_control,
        "kill_checks": kills,
        "verdict": "dev_pass" if not any(kills.values()) else "fail",
        "timing": ("RSP/SPY daily closes through session t; target set at the "
                   "close of t, filled at the first bar open of t+1; 2% band; "
                   "long only."),
        "notes": ("RSP and SPY adjusted closes are read from data/external/ "
                  "and reindexed to the QQQ session calendar.  The development "
                  "run ends 2023-12-29 and does not load 2024-2026 prices."),
    }
    H.write_result(Path(__file__).with_name("result.json"), payload)
    print(f"{SLUG}: {H.summary_line(st)}")
    print("  10bp:", H.summary_line(ev["stats"]["10bp"]))
    print("  corr range", payload["corr_range"], "verdict", payload["verdict"])
    print("  kills", [k for k, v in kills.items() if v])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
